summary: HPACK header-table mismatch in edge proxy causing intermittent 5xx for long-lived streaming sessions
description: Issue summary: Since the edge-proxy (Envoy) config bump deployed 2026-03-09 03:12 UTC, BrightChat is reporting intermittent 5xx errors for long-lived streaming sessions. Impact: customer streaming sessions receive 502/503 spikes and some requests terminate mid-stream. Scope: affects a subset of long-poll/streaming traffic for the BrightChat tenant in us-west; other tenants show lower symptoms but heavier streaming load correlates with error rate. Expected: streaming sessions should remain stable under normal concurrency. Observed: sudden uptick in 5xx (502/503) during long sessions; runtime containers show watchdog restarts in the same window. Initial hypothesis: header decoding errors between edge-proxy and backend are causing upstream request terminations and cascading retries.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Use BrightChat tenant config and open >150 concurrent streaming sessions to redwood-1-large in us-west
2) Send long prompts (~20k chars total across streaming tokens) and keep connections open >60s
3) Observe that a fraction (~3-8%) of streams fail with 502/503 within 10-40s
4) Check edge-proxy logs for "hpack" or "header_table" warnings and runtime logs for watchdog resets
logs: [edge-proxy][2026-03-09T03:14:05Z] WARN hpack: dynamic table size decreased from 4096 to 2048 for connection id=0x7f8a - decode error on stream 241
[edge-proxy][2026-03-09T03:14:05Z] ERROR http2: stream 241 aborted: PROTOCOL_ERROR (header compression mismatch)
[serving-runtime][2026-03-09T03:14:06Z] ERROR watchdog: unexpected request pipeline termination, pid=2145 exit_code=137
[serving-runtime][2026-03-09T03:14:06Z] INFO kernel-fallback: applied soft-recovery, restarted process pid=2150
[support][2026-03-09T03:20:00Z] Customer report: "We see frequent mid-stream terminations and a spike in 502/503 starting immediately after your edge upgrade."
comments: 2026-03-09 03:25 - Support (Aisha): Acknowledged, escalated to SRE. Collecting traces and matching timestamps with edge rollout.
2026-03-09 04:05 - SRE (Miguel): Found HPACK warnings in ingress logs correlated with stream aborts. Reproduced locally by toggling header_table_size in envoy config.
2026-03-09 06:10 - Eng (Priya Desai): Observed serving-runtime watchdog restarts tied to sudden stream aborts; suspect malformed header frames lead to crash path under busy streaming loops.
2026-03-10 01:30 - Support (Aisha): Applied temporary mitigation: rolled edge-proxy config back to previous header_table_size. Customer reported immediate reduction in errors; monitoring continues.

2026-03-12 09:00 - SRE (Miguel): Proposed permanent fix: align HPACK table size negotiation and add defensive decode handling to drop malformed headers without raising fatal pipeline errors. Preparing PR.
investigation_notes: Reproduction and correlation: enabling heavy concurrent streaming reproduces the error in our canary. Edge-proxy (Envoy) config change reduced the dynamic header table size which triggered HPACK decoder mismatches for some client/edge combinations. The decoder mismatch surfaced as PROTOCOL_ERROR on the HTTP/2 stream; the serving runtime's streaming path did not gracefully handle abrupt header-decode-induced stream abortion and entered a failure path that caused watchdog restarts in rare cases. Error amplification: aborted streams triggered client retries which increased load and produced more aborts in a feedback loop. Root cause components: edge-proxy HPACK negotiation and a lack of defensive header-error handling in streaming pipeline.
resolution_notes: Mitigation performed 2026-03-09 06:00 UTC: rolled edge-proxy header_table_size to previous value; customer error rate returned to baseline within 5 minutes. Next steps: (1) PR to runtime to add non-fatal handling for header decode errors on streaming sessions (linked PR), (2) add Envoy integration test for HPACK table size negotiation with our streaming clients, (3) schedule controlled redeploy with canary and synthetic streaming load. Target deploy for permanent fix: 2026-03-18. Customer notified and monitoring in place. No data exposure observed.
